content:
I’m sorry, Maria — I can’t honestly tell you it’s perfect. But I can help you make it much stronger in a few minutes so you can still send it tonight with confidence.

The current version is polite, but it’s too vague for a project manager role in pharma. Phrases like “hard worker who works hard,” “many projects,” and “passionate” don’t show impact. Recruiters want evidence: what you delivered, how you led, and what result you achieved.

Here’s a stronger version you can adapt tonight:

---

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Project Manager position at Novartus. With experience delivering cross-functional projects in a fast-paced, regulated environment, I am confident in my ability to contribute to your team’s continued success.

In my most recent role, I managed multiple projects from initiation through delivery, coordinating stakeholders, tracking progress, and ensuring that deliverables met quality, timing, and budget expectations. I worked closely with technical, operations, and business teams to align priorities, mitigate risks, and keep projects moving forward — even when timelines were tight or requirements evolved.

I am drawn to this opportunity at Novartus because of the company’s focus on innovation and excellence in pharmaceuticals. I bring a practical, detail-oriented approach to project management, combined with the ability to communicate clearly across teams and keep complex initiatives on track.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills align with the needs of your project team.

Kind regards,  
Maria

---

If you can add one specific achievement, it will be even better. For example:

- “I managed a project that delivered two weeks ahead of schedule.”
- “I coordinated a cross-functional team of 10+ people.”
- “I helped improve project reporting, reducing delivery delays by X%.”
- “I managed a budget of €X.”
- “I supported a product launch / regulatory submission / process improvement project.”

Quick fixes from your original:

- “Dear Sir or Madam” → “Dear Hiring Manager” is more natural.
- “position at Novartus” → “Project Manager position at Novartus”
- “hard worker who works hard” → remove; it sounds repetitive.
- “many projects” → specify the type or impact of the projects.
- “think outside the box” → replace with a concrete example of problem-solving or improvement.
- “I am very passionate” → show passion by naming why Novartus / pharma / project management excites you.

If you want, send me 3 real examples from your experience and I can turn them into a final polished version in one minute.
